fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Supreme Court Review 2024: Batting for bail in the face of delayed trials - Supreme Court Observer
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Home > Analysis > Supreme Court Review 2024: Batting for bail in the face of delayed trials. # Supreme Court Review 2024: Batting for bail in the face of delayed trials. Yet, 2024 saw the Supreme Court soften its stance in several high-profile cases, where it relied on prolonged incarceration and the long road to trial as a factor for granting bail. In 2024, the Supreme Court granted bail to former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal on three separate occasions following his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in connection with the Delhi Liquor Policy scam. His CBI arrest came immediately after a trial court had granted him bail in the ED case. Justice Bhuyan noted that the CBI had been investigating Kejriwal and the Delhi Liquor Policy scam for over a year but only deemed it necessary to arrest him when he was on the verge of release in the ED case.

PMLA is nothing but Pradhan Mantri Ki Lal Aankh: Kapil Sibal on prevention of money laundering act
The Economic Times
3460000 subscribers
27 likes
1546 views
22 May 2024
Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal claimed that the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) stands for 'Pradhan Mantri ki Lal Ankh' and has nothing to do with money laundering. He explained that the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), the law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing economic laws in the country, can arrest any accused based on any oral statement. Watch!
